ateret-zekenim/1:א: (א) It is open to itself and the vacant Soma that is not lit in his house and he is in a room by himself is obliged to light Hanukkah candles as I wrote above in the sign of 1911, section 8:
ateret-zekenim/1:ב: (ב) that he eats (see words of Orach Chayim s.k. 7) and concludes: since known to all they kindle in winter house where they do not eat, and known each has nearby immediately by eating place a sleeping place — sleeping place is called well for kindling in sleeping place; but one who eats occasionally once or even regularly and sleeping place is far from eating place — then kindle in sleeping place; see further in Shaarei Yeshuvah siman 73. Per the distinction I wrote, both are upheld — Rama's Hagahah and words of Chami Zekeni Maharari cited above.
ateret-zekenim/3:א: (א) that make light of him, etc. 11. A person who lights a Hanukkah candle in his house on him (the response of the Rama C. 20 in the opinion of the column):
ateret-zekenim/3:ב: (ב) And blesses them, and there are some who disagree (Maharash) and above doubt blessings to make it easier only if you want to make it worse because it will be lit without a blessing as above:
ateret-zekenim/4:_: Makes a bonfire for him. It appears all leftover oil even more than kindling measure — only oil in the candle designated for kindling requires bonfire as Bach wrote siman 66 — end; so explicitly Ran Bava Metzia and Tosafot chapter Kirah; so Avudraham in name of Rabbenu Shlomo; also another answer: Chazal equated it to holy utensils because reminder of holy oil. What Bach questioned — Beit Yosef wrote in siman 672 if he put more he may extinguish after time passed and may use afterward, etc. — appears difference: certainly may extinguish to kindle other candles and use its light; nevertheless must burn in manner requiring genizah as Avudraham — examine per this Bach's strains unnecessary — this appears plain, finding most poskim agree — Bach's strain void — examine. Some say leftover from day one kindle immediately night two — at end no remedy; also delaying forbidden lest mishap; nevertheless not called shiluach; nullified in sixty; less than sixty no nullification even by kindling. What ruled above after kindling measure may extinguish and do as he wishes — speaks where he put more than measure; where only measure and it went out or wick bad and tangled — forbidden (Rashal siman 85); however what he wrote even if put more requires genizah as I wrote for halacha.
biur-halacha/1:א: (א) To give a penny to the Ba'ab - refer to the M.B. Mishka in the guy next to the table in the Ba'ab Dach to participate is from the words of Magan Avraham [and not from the words of the Rashel] and refer to Farah Deldidiya in all its shades one should participate and what the Magan Avraham brought evidence from the words of the Ria in the name of Och for the matter of the son of the neighbor because his father the Meiri brought in the name of the Sages of the Tosaf a model for this one should participate and even to the Meiri who disagrees there about them cf. In Dina Dhamma, he certainly thanks them, and we need to participate in his words:
biur-halacha/1:ב: (ב) to participate, etc. - and one should be careful with this sharing that he does not light it one night and the other night, but rather let the oil be shared every night or give him a penny to earn him a share in all the nights [from Iri in the name of the Sages of the Tosafs]:
biur-halacha/1:ג: (ג) With him, etc. — see Peri Megadim Orach Chayim letter 3: if two householders in one room and do not rely on each other and each eats his own — requires study if partnership suffices, perhaps each must kindle by law; guest perhaps they were lenient — end; letter 8 brought Levush and Peri Chadash dispute; see Peri Chadash proofs from Maggid Mishneh chapter 4 Hanukkah laws must kindle; from Shibolei Leket Hanukkah siman 185 in name of our rabbis — from his conclusion implies since in one house partnership suffices.
biur-halacha/1:ד: (ד) An opening, etc. - apparently because the taste is because of the suspicion of passers-by and returnees, so in our time they light up inside the house, like this suspicion, and as the Bahjah wrote at the end of the sign of 131 and Amai Mahmirinan, he has an open door, although later I found in the Mahri'al in the sign of KMA, the opposite of what I said, that means there, in the simplicity of his language, the Idna, that they light up everything inside the house, because every guest even knew, of course, that his wife was lighting At his home, for him, a MM should light a blood in the hostel for himself knowing that he is married and his wife lights it for him in his home and him for her suspicions. For Shifarin) and it's hard for the Rama from Mn I.S.L. as Haril Dehashta, because the litikin in the face was a tiff, he had to read it in our hands even if there is no open opening, he should light it for himself, and if not S.L.
biur-halacha/1:ה: (ה) Open - we are satisfied if the house is not even separated from it, but the guest has one corner in the house that he uses there and at that corner he has an opening to the street that he enters and leaves through there and they will be suspicious when he does not turn on the light for himself or if I imagine that the house is divided from it and he has a special room there, then they will be suspicious and it also apparently means the language of the Shu'a from the end of his words. This is how it is in the Sheba'l, a KFA sign that there are two views on this, and a little bit:
biur-halacha/1:ו: (ו) To himself - see MB. And in order for you to understand the source of my words, I have to copy the language of the protector Avraham and Zal and Idna, who lighten inside, even guests lighten (the law of the Hari'u C. 11a and the Haril, see KM5) and precisely when I am eating in the room in the P.E. That the truth is with AR and behold, I labored a lot on the words of the defender Avraham Or Yisrael, how could he make a mistake in this. And I later found by glossing over the Shabbat additions on the Okh at the end of Aish and it is proven from his words that Hagan Avraham intended to order that there is not even an open door for himself, except when he eats in the room in Pe. And here is really an opinion from the Rivu and the Haril to be stricter in all aspects, but the opinion of the defender Avraham to instruct according to their method when I can eat in the room in the P.A.F.A.P. and P.Z.
biur-halacha/1:ז: (ז) Where I can eat - see MB Mashak Demi who dines at his friend at random and has a house there, in the same city, etc. And precisely in this way, but if he and all the members of his household go to his father's or father-in-law's house regularly on the 8th day of Hanukkah, it is clear that since he dines and sleeps there all the days of Hanukkah, even though during the day he eats naked food in his house, he does not light it, but in the house where he eats and sleeps there at night, since there is no one in the house to whom to light it, and the Idna that is known to the members of the household and since the members of the household sleep there, they will light it [Parach.
biur-halacha/3:_: and light it in the PA, etc. - the HA wrote, according to what was explained above, the main time to light it is only until it wears out and it is known that the travelers to the fairs travel for several hours at night, therefore it is appropriate for every Yarish to warn his wife before his journey to be careful about lighting the light as soon as the stars come out and he will trust them and when he comes to Oshfiza he will light it without a blessing and boast of hearing the blessings from the one who must light it and he will answer Amen (his opinion) per the opinion of the Rashel and the Farah). ACL:
biur-halacha/4:א: (א) From the oil, etc. - refer to 22, that is, when it was extinguished in the middle of the lesson, and if such an one was extinguished on the night of Zain and on the night of the 8th, much more oil than the lesson was added and fuel for about half an hour's lesson, and what is left over seems to be forbidden from enjoying them, of course there is some of the oil inside the forbidden Zain, unless one knows that the oil he added to the night before was S against the first bit:
biur-halacha/4:ב: (ב) It is necessary, etc. - refer to 22 Mishka Dish Poskim Shasoverin, etc. But if he took a saucer of oil for a Hanukkah candle and uses it to consume it for the OT, the remaining oil in the Hanukkah candle is not permitted at all:
biur-halacha/4:ג: (ג) For the ignition rate - the Shag wrote that if the oil gave the ignition rate half an hour and the fuel more than half an hour (such as the wick was thin and he thought the wick was medium), if it is permissible to be satisfied with it, then it is allowed since it is an action of his own free will, even if it is accidental, it is prohibited. And his words were quoted in MA:
chatam-sofer/1:_: In the MGA, Section 12, and no fees for the 16th mark. P.S. See above C. Tamma Sasakah:
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: (Seif 1) Guest on whom they do not kindle, etc. NB: See third responsum — since Moharit's words strengthened, etc.; see my essays on Avodah Zarah daf 68a proof for Moharit's view and our explanation inside Sefer HaChaim resolving Maharshal's difficulty on Rashi d.h. le'itot erev — see and examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (Ibid. Section 2) A child who has come to education should be lit. P.S. I was satisfied with the child who increased within the days of Hanukkah and a resident who converted within 8 days of Hanukkah whether or not he is obligated to allow the candles. And ATL is obligated if we convert at night after a foot has been consumed from the market dkyl in retrospect. And here the Maga wrote in the name of the GMI in C. 1555 Degar that we were converted before the hot hawk is exempted from reciting the night and the main mitzvah by day. And here we see that the main mitzvah of the day is not to exempt from the night recitation Dabeza Mai Iria if it is the main mitzvah on the day of Efi' If the main mitzvah is at night or a sine Nami is exempted from the night recitation in this since it precedes the hot hawk, it is a day and the night recitation does not belong to it except through Tishlomin and since it is exempted during its obligation it is also exempted afterwards and as many as the rulings yes Gabi Onan in the Havdalah. And in the ML the meaning is that the main mitzvah is the day. But the meaning is that the main mitzvah is not the main mitzvah of the day. They are exempted on the day because it is not all of the day. But since the main mitzvah of the day is still the whole of the day, it is the meaning of this, that we converted before the hot hawk. We are exempted from the night prayer. Exemption also due to day. And if so, on Hanukkah, all the days are equal, he would appear to be completely exempt, since he did not spend all his time in obligation, and at the time the obligation began, he would be exempt. Who looks Daino Dham at Purim Oh, the miracle before the 14th and 14th was already a day of rest and is not just a memory of the yesterday's miracle. Therefore, if the main part of the mitzvah was not performed on the day and not all of it was performed on the day, they would be exempt from the day. But since DKIL diminishes time and it does not diminish a miracle as Damperes in the Shas, Dans every day with it, and if so the the Master in this, then the miracle is every day a new miracle and must be blessed for the coming. And here in this it would seem to understand the philogta what Dafligi Amorii in Tama Dvash and Bh Dahd SAL Dtama Dvsh against the incoming days and Tama Dvah against the outgoing days. And HA tama divash against the fruit of the holiday and tama divah from power above in the holy place, etc. And apparently what is not acceptable to Dinah Hoi in this. But per the above 11 dnm for a converted and small ger who increased in the middle of the days of Hanukkah, here is the taste of Dvash against the incoming days, the resident must also light per the value of the incoming Hanukkah days for every person. But the Omnipresent is dimmed against the outwards, because in the outwards it is not a burden, and that has no relevance to the strictness of it and lights only a different candle, or because it is not possible against the outwards, it is acknowledged that the Omnipresent is dimly lit against the inward. And indeed, the more it is possible to light against the going out, the more it is lit, but the more it is not possible to acknowledge the Omnipresent, the more it is lit against the entering. And in this will be the division between the reasons. But if he started in the middle and didn't light it at all, the whole payment is not similar to the fruit of the holiday, so he admits that he is liable for it at all. to be holy. And there will be a good adversary between the tastes of the taste against the outgoing or the entering, then to the the Master we will be converted and the small one who increased will light up as much as a person against the entering. And the LB is faded against the vechiin in a gar, it doesn't belong, yes, this is a sl dain, in which it is compiled at all. Or Damdlik against the entrance. And on the other hand, there is a reason against the fruit of the holiday and being exalted in the holy place, to reverse the old and small rabbis that we are committed to in the middle, there is no complicity in it at all since our day is similar to the fruit of the holiday. As mentioned above. And it is fair to me that the Harif and the Rash copied the phlogta of Taam in the 2nd and 2nd. And apparently there is no nam for the dina in it. And per the above, Shafir has an enemy in him. Who, being so, is a deger that we convert in the middle and a small one that increased in the middle must be reviewed if we convert or the increased are considered according to their hours in other years that consumed a leg from the market whether it is due on the same night or not. And apparently it would seem that since his main time was only until a leg was spent from the market, and then he was for payment, so if at the time of his main obligation he was exempt, then he must light it later, and he was, as they say in the Magellan, a waiver from reading the night and onan in the Havdalah. I light an ann for a shifra and why not from two dnm to a resident that we will convert after a time that will be consumed, etc. A dept from lighting the night is only for payments and never another person will I not light a light later in the Torah tishlomin and also for a shira Nami not in our eyes and not in the night only later oh only For payments and a resident who converts or the minor who lit is exempt from this night, the hours and hours are calculated according to this:
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: (Same, seif 3) In Hagahah: even if he lodges with gentiles and sees candles, if he wants to be stringent, etc. NB: See Taz who extended; now clear proof for those who forbid stringency from what we learn Berachot 33: difficult — if so say when he makes havdalah on this and not on that, blessings fall on his head; why challenge — say certainly make havdalah on cup not at all in prayer — prayer certainly preferable to cup; only if he makes havdalah in prayer without intent to fulfill, only on cup being d'rabbanan no intent needed; nevertheless if intends not to fulfill — certainly not fulfilled; so truly regarding counting siman 489 — counts with congregation without blessing, intends not to fulfill, blesses later at night — Magen Avraham proves even if intent not required, if intends not to fulfill — not fulfilled though counting then. If so here fits: blessings fall on his head since he truly made havdalah in prayer and on cup — blessing in vain since he intended fulfill havdalah in prayer; nevertheless did not change prayer wording since he also mentioned in prayer — he is among mehaderin; but if he did not make havdalah in prayer at all — worse one who makes havdalah on cup than prayer without cup — why challenge? Must prove like Tosefet Yehuda: if he could have fulfilled through prayer havdalah since he made havdalah again — blessing in vain; not so counting when day and cannot fulfill then. Clear proof in my view. When there I wondered greatly why challenge — perhaps intent: one who makes havdalah on this and that means if first on cup then prayer — blessings fall since then not vain; why challenge? Must be intent: then interruption in prayer — difficult on Rabbeinu Yona Bach Orach Chayim 108 brought mentioning other days' events in prayer is not interruption — learned from if he made havdalah in both he fulfilled; here havdalah must be interruption. Without Rabbeinu Yona — no proof from havdalah — certainly mentioning matter evident not of the day is interruption since evident it is interruption; but havdalah at night — if he did not pray at all he could make havdalah in this prayer — not evident from prayer body it is interruption — not known if he prayed; therefore not evident from body is not interruption. This is Taz's objection; I explained his reason more; even so our question remains: in havdalah on cup first also not evident if already made havdalah on cup — therefore appears main distinction: there prayer draws prayer — if not prayer time no place to pray makeup only because prayer time therefore prays makeup too — obligatory prayer time causes second prayer — one prayer considered; support from generally once permission given, given; not interruption; but if say he made havdalah on cup — no need havdalah in prayer — no havdalah in prayer; if made havdalah — interruption; challenge well. If say like R' Yonah who holds wherever mentioning event matter — not interruption even without this reason — challenge well: why not say intent if first on cup; requires study; proves like Taz not Rabbeinu Yona — examine. Regarding dispute where to begin kindling — see my essays Yoreh De'ah 4th edition siman 280 end daf 162 explanation of Gemara language so mezuzah on right — see and examine well.
chokhmat-shlomo/4:_: (Same, seif 4) Leftover on eighth day of oil for kindling measure, etc. NB: What all found Shulchan Aruch contradictory — see darush Hanukkah year 5560 resolving distinction between prohibition matter and mitzvah matter — see there with God's help. Regarding what all found contradictory to siman 672 — Taz in name of Moharai brought answer: here unspecified oil, there he stipulated only kindling measure; Taz wondered from Gemara chapter Nigmar hadin what he does not see he does not grasp — like Abaye in invitation so Rava in action; we wrote above from this. Now appears per our novellae in Sukkah laws [still in manuscript] to prove not like Hagahot R' Yehoshua Magen Avraham brought — sukkah not forbidden until one sits — invitation not a matter; I proved from what we say: if he set aside seven etrogim for seven days, each fulfills with it and eats next day; if invitation not a matter — in Beit HaShanah not muktzeh — no muktzeh for half Shabbat — why not permitted immediately? Must be invitation is a matter; reason: since sukkah forbidden in benefit from festival "what is festival to God" — in invitation and body of holiness it is a matter as Magen Avraham siman 42; so sukkah; so lulav since we learn lulav from sukkah — see there; so Hanukkah light since similar to menorah as Rashi d.h. hadlakah oseh mitzvah similar to menorah — invitation matter like body of holiness; therefore fits Abaye in invitation alone since only speech not act — what he does not see he does not grasp; so Rava in action with these invitations not a matter — when only act we say why he sees we count act; for permitted part act not counted — end act not done in permitted at all. Here with oil — by invitation alone also forbidden; invitation at act time applies to all — did not know if needed or which part permitted — invitation on all; again if act afterward since invitation and act here all forbidden; act on part helps whole since he invited all — one body; act on part helps whole since invited all; invitation makes one entity; act on stronger part helps whole; all agree; Mechaber's words fit; need not say there stipulated, there without prior invitation only act — Taz's view what he does not see he does not grasp; here he invited all first then kindled — with invitation and act all forbidden; She'iltot source all poskim concluded: since designated for mitzvah why all this — known forbidden from start; intent teaches designated from start with invitation and act together — fits — examine; such my leaning now. Support for distinction: Choshen Mishpat siman 275 seif 7 and Sema — holding gentile property does not acquire until removes bundle and returns; if called on gentile's name acquires all called on his name — see there; so if invitation is matter and all called Hanukkah light — act on part helps all called on its name — see there; if no invitation act on oil does not help rest — examine. Magen Avraham and Peri Chadash forbid keeping for next year lest mishap — difficult: proof there Torah prohibition therefore decree mishap; Hanukkah is itself rabbinic prohibition — why mishap concern — decree on decree? See darush Hanukkah cited — I proved also from this they made like Torah law because of blessing — examine. May leftover oil in Hanukkah lamp be kindled in synagogue to pray by it? Plainly permitted — forbidden in benefit nevertheless mitzvot not given for benefit; even for those holding even rabbinic mitzvot not for benefit — only Torah benefit prohibitions we follow Torah obligation; not obligated in this mitzvah — benefits from Torah like eino metzuveh ve'oseh. Rabbinic benefit prohibition — permitted to fulfill their mitzvah; if follow Torah — permitted entirely; if rabbinic — rabbinically commanded and in matter commanded upon him not for benefit. Hanukkah light from their words — permitted holy use; also in Hanukkah itself some permit holy use; forbidders only while burning for mitzvah — lest holy use not recognizable; or bizuy mitzvah from mitzvah to mitzvah; if remainder burned alone — clear recognition, no bizuy — burning only because forbidden in benefit more bizuy than lighting in synagogue; see Taz similar above siman 154 — even lowering from holiness only if still fit for mitzvah; if not fit — better light mitzvah than genizah; all the more here better holy use than burying — plain to me, need not write; since Peri Megadim in Mishbetzot wrote opposite and permitted only by addition — wrote to remove from that book's heart; in Machatzit HaShekel great error, not as he wrote — examine. (Same seif) Some say may not add to nullify — NB: see my responsum year 5553 Shulchan Aruch Yoreh De'ah siman 69 goose fat law — examine well.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [a] [clothing] and who is in a penny, etc. And we were with Didahu but not with Didan (Mahiri 6, Seaman 31), and he also wrote in the answer of the Maharil, Seaman 16, and the Idna, most of the time, there is no participation and taama because of suspicion, so far, and the ways of Moses and Rashel, Seaman 55, were permitted even at this time. And here in the Magan Avraham wrote from the Rilo and Haril Meiri when he eats in a room by himself, and it is not true that he wrote from the Rial to Mai Danhog the Idna to light each and every one if so it is for Mimishtha and all her guests to light demi mephis to know if he is married and his wife lights him or a young man and is lit in the BH, and in the rest of the Great Knesset the participant should hear the blessings from the consecrator if he does not have to bless the vision:
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [b] and participant etc. I have heard that it is necessary to add what his friend (Aguda) will give, the interpretation of Dam is not evident that he added for his friend I have a suspicion, and according to this he did not even add everything that he gave him except for a little bit of Sagi Danicher who participated in what he added on top of what was usual (BH). Therefore, it seems reasonable to me that the lighter is obliged to give a half-hourly lesson from his own money, refer to Sign 136, to which one should add that if he does not, he did not give to fulfill his obligation. The Rashba wrote, Sign 1942, which is the law if the owner of the house gives him a portion of the sherry oil as a gift:
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [c] Where I can eat, etc. We were regulars, but at the meal that was eaten at his friend's house, it is a random mitzvah from the chosen one that he should go to his house and light it, and in hindsight, when his wife lights a seg for him and wherever he is, one should bless the sight at the place where he dines at his friend's house (Bah). If he heard the blessings from the owner of the house and answers Amen, one should not bless the sight (remains of the Great Knesset), and one should say Demeiri that the owner of the house should go out to him:
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [d] [wearing] the authority in his hand, etc. And they also practice (Rama), and Rashel Siman 55 ruled like Beit Yosef that he is not to bless unless it is known that it was lit on him, and it is difficult for me on the Shear of Ephraim Siman 22 that wrote that Beit Yosef to her taste all the members of his household light one, but per the custom of a Didan for all scholars one should bless that in general, the strict one up to this point. In the answer of the Maharil, mark Kanu, and in the Maharil, he wrote to Hai Danhigi to light every member of his household, etc., because of a blessing to cancel it. There is no such thing here, since Dainu wants to go out because of his wife, so far, he has been given a gift from the mahadrin like the rest of his household, I also wrote in the sign of 131 seq. 2 Da'ish and his wife is not at all a mahadrin as one imagined body. He will stand by the owner of the house when he blesses and answer Amen, and if the owner of the house has already lit the light, he will bless without the name of the kingdom, as Moses decreed, and I say Dain to protest our customs and as they testified from the Ri'u and the Haril that I brought:
eshel-avraham/1:_: at his father's. See T. B. D. Siman 1873:
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: A) [Section 1] An innkeeper who does not have a Medlakin on him in his house, etc. apparently it would seem to interpret the Madlakin on him in two ways. In the opinion of the late Maimonides, the late Rambam says that all the members of the house light a candle, the island is lit for him, a rabbi who lights a candle for him in his house, as if he were standing there, and according to other judges (Desbri, a candle is a person and his house), a rabbi who lights a candle inside his house, meaning that his wife lights a candle, and he goes out with it 18 when lighting it, but per the words of the Gaon Ha'el 14, mark 11, and the words of the rest of the latter, the latter does not mean the most and is not must From AMR Letter A and refer to above C. 1991 O. V.:
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (ב) There. Must give perutah, etc. — precise to say perutah: guest need not give half candle cost — perutah given suffices. Some say in Hagahot. Mishna Berurah letter 3: when giving perutah say: I give you this perutah so you acquire for me some oil and wicks in your Hanukkah lights you kindle tonight, or if he wishes all eight nights; homeowner says: I transfer to you some oil with this perutah in my Hanukkah lights I kindle all eight nights. Without perutah homeowner may transfer if he wishes as below letter 5 — say I transfer to you, etc., stand by him at blessing, intend to fulfill through homeowner's blessing; homeowner also intends to discharge him as known.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (ג) There. Must give perutah, etc. — appears guest giving expense to homeowner — then must participate; if special room must kindle in room; if guest relies entirely on homeowner — eats from his bread, drinks from his cup — no need, for homeowner who provides all needs will also transfer part of candle money — no suspicion since known he relies on homeowner. Gan HaMelech siman 41. Some say there Shaarei Teshuvah letter 1 Shulchan Gavoah letter 2 in Machatzit — if eats with homeowner on account of all he eats and drinks — needs perutah; if eats as contractor so much per day or week for all needs — no perutah. Appears likewise if homeowner gives all free — no perutah; nevertheless better explicitly say transfer some oil in your Hanukkah lights and homeowner says I transfer, etc., whether paid or free; however what wrote even with special room need not kindle — see below letter 9 — appears same here.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: d) I wrote in the association that I heard that a person who shares with his friend in the Nah should add what his friend will give him. And his taste is not evident that he added for his friend Icha Susda to say that we will not participate and PZ Efi' did not add everything he gave him except for a little Nemi Segi Danicher who will participate in what he added on top of what was usual. BH. Neighbor 3 in the GHT letter B. MA SKA. And which of the words of the A.R. letter 2 means that he should give oil for the innkeeper as a half-hourly rate for the innkeeper, as in Mash Aa letter A, and the Parah wrote a DAC to add to the candle what he gave him and the Mash Bah to add a little, not to be afraid of Yaush. Although the DAH letter 2 ruled, per the words of the Bah Daba'2, one should add a little oil for the guest in addition to the rate that should be given for half an hour. And cf. MB letter 3 and wrote Vadla as the AR. And cf.
levushei-serad/1:_: MA DHA Kat. Essiman 1772, etc. A real witness can light up at night:
levushei-serad/2:_: Section 503 — the laws of Mahariv brought in Darkei Moshe 2; nowadays one does not participate with a perutah even if he has no open door for himself. Magen Avraham explains that he eats in a room alone; therefore in Talmudic times when they kindled at the entrance from outside, since there was only one entrance, participation suffices — not so nowadays when they kindle inside, and since there are two rooms he must kindle alone; but when there is no room alone, even nowadays participation suffices. However on the face of the matter it does not appear so; there is to resolve — requires study.
levushei-serad/3:_: MA SKO even the Rash is the information brought by the author per the fact that at that time the the Master still made light in front of the door of the house inside, but at this time he admits, and so on, Sassiman 1515 in MA Ski'd.
levushei-serad/4:_: {Rama: s.k. 4} As siman 671, etc. In courtyard with two openings — kindle at both, bless only at one not second since only suspicion.
